text:
Jett Washington could have played basketball.

He was good enough. He helped Bishop Gorman in Las Vegas win back to back Nevada state basketball championships. College programs wanted him on the hardwood.

His uncle was Kobe Bryant.

He picked football instead.

Washington is a five star safety, ranked the best in the country at his position in the 2026 class. He's 6-foot-5 and 210 pounds, which is roughly tight end size, playing in the secondary.

Oregon's defensive coordinator Chris Hampton put it plainly on signing day.

"He's got the best height-weight-speed combination in all of high school football."

Thirty programs offered him. He cut it to eleven, then to three, and picked Oregon over Alabama and USC.

Athletics run both directions in his family. His mother Sharia is Kobe's older sister. His father Jerrod Washington played running back at Virginia and was drafted by the Patriots back in 1994.

Here's the part that says the most about him.

Washington chose the one sport where nobody could measure him against Kobe.

Then in March he announced his Oregon jersey number.

Twenty four.

He also wears a purple and gold mouthguard, and a Black Mamba shirt under his pads.

He's talked about the weight that comes with the name, and how his family handles it.

"Sometimes I feel a little bit of pressure being his nephew, but my parents make sure I don't feel it too much. They tell me to just go out there and have fun, don't try to overthink and just play."

Then he said the thing that explains the whole choice.

"My uncle was a great player. At the same time, I know he wanted me to make my own name. He laid the foundation for me. I'm just grateful."

Asked what he remembers most about Kobe, it wasn't anything about basketball.

"Just the positive energy and positive vibes he had."

He's a freshman at Oregon now, running out of the tunnel at Autzen with 24 on his back, in a sport his uncle never played.

🚨🏍️ DPS Seeks Driver Who Fled After Fatal Motorcycle Crash in Grayson County 🏍️🚨

Grayson County, TX — The Texas Department of Public Safety is asking for the public’s help identifying the driver of a Toyota Corolla involved in a fatal July crash near Sherman.

The crash occurred around 2:51 p.m. July 22 at US-82 and Smith Oak Road in unincorporated Grayson County.

According to DPS, a preliminary investigation indicates a motorcycle was traveling eastbound on US-82 when the driver of the Toyota Corolla failed to yield the right of way to the motorcycle.

The motorcycle operator was transported to Texoma Medical Center, where he later died from his injuries. A passenger on the motorcycle was hospitalized with serious injuries.

DPS said the driver of the Toyota Corolla fled following the crash and is now being sought by authorities.

💰 REWARD OFFERED

North Texas Crime Stoppers is offering a reward of up to $5,000 for information leading to the arrest and indictment of the Toyota Corolla driver.

🕵️ HOW TO SUBMIT A TIP
